Channel ready.

title: Role Assignment
text:
Role assigned: Manager of the OWECS Project.

Location: Ministry of Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Ocean Affairs.
Republic of Arcadia.

Project: Offshore Wind Energy in the Conan Sea (OWECS).
Welcome. I will brief you on Arcadia's energy situation and the OWECS project before we consult the stakeholders.

title: Background — Arcadia
text:
Arcadia is a highly industrialised and densely populated country, strategically positioned as a transit hub for global goods transportation.

It has a thriving export sector in agricultural products and chemicals, alongside a small-scale fishing industry integral to local communities.

title: Background — Energy Challenge
text:
Arcadia's economy relies heavily on substantial energy consumption. To align with the Paris Agreement and the SDGs, it must reduce its dependence on fossil fuels and strive towards net zero emissions.

Arcadia has an extensive coastline, making offshore wind parks a promising avenue for renewable energy — contributing to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

title: Background — Expected Benefits
text:
The OWECS wind park is expected to:
- Generate ~50% of the energy required to sustain local industry
- Satisfy 10% of household energy demands using residual industrial heat
- Provide 30% of the electricity needed to power Arcadia's trains

The proposed location is within Arcadia's territorial sea.
The precise design of the wind park is not yet set in stone. Our Ministry attaches great importance to a balanced approach that considers the views of all stakeholders.

title: Guiding Principle
text:
Given the limited space available, equitable and multifunctional use of space is needed, creating an equilibrium between economic, social and ecological needs.

The area reserved for wind turbines must also contribute to other economic, social and ecological objectives.

As you assess mitigation measures, keep two questions in mind:

1. Which measures should be implemented to reach an optimal result — the least possible trade-offs between relevant SDGs?

2. Are your solutions in conformity with Arcadia's obligations under international law?

Top scores go to measures that reduce trade-offs the most while remaining in line with international law. Review the case materials, examine the project area, and consider what a balanced response could look like.

title: Objective Updated
text:
- Review each Point of Interest on the map
- Hear stakeholder concerns and legal perspectives
- Choose mitigation measures that balance the SDGs

title: Point of Interest: Ramsar Wetland (SDG 15)
text: The wetland is protected under the Ramsar Convention and hosts more than 20,000 migratory birds, including the critically endangered red knot (Calidris canutus), listed in Annex I of the Bonn Convention.

title: Phase 1 — Exploration
text: Hear from the stakeholders about the potential impacts on the wetland and migratory birds.

The project cannot be realised in this part of the Conan sea. It is too close to the wetland, which is protected under the Ramsar Convention and hosts more than 20,000 migratory birds that use this site to rest on their long journeys. These include the red knot (Calidris canutus), a critically endangered species listed in Annex I of the Bonn Convention.

The construction noise could drive the red knot out permanently. There is also a significant risk of bird collision with the turbine blades during operation. The project thus negatively impacts SDG 15. Arcadia furthermore breaches its obligations under the Ramsar and Bonn Conventions if it decides to go ahead with the project.
Arcadia does indeed have obligations to protect migratory birds under the Bonn Convention, especially towards endangered species such as the red knot.

The possible negative impacts of wind parks on migratory birds have been recognized by the COP, which has called on parties to act with precaution in the development of wind turbine parks. Arcadia is equally under an obligation to protect the ecological character of the wetland pursuant to the Ramsar Convention, but it can delete or restrict the boundaries of a listed wetland if it is “in its urgent national interest”.

title: Phase 2 — Intervention
text: You have three options to reduce bird fatalities. Combining options 1 and 2 provides the best outcome.

Which measure 
would you like to implement?

options.label: Painting the rotor blades (in bright colours)
Seasonal shutdown of the wind turbines

title: Option: Paint Rotor Blades
text: Painting the rotor blades in bright colours makes them more visible to birds.
Good idea! With the rotor blades becoming more visible, bird mortality will be reduced with 80%.

This is a good and affordable option, but is it sufficient in light of our obligations under the Ramsar and Bonn Conventions? I also foresee legal claims from the tourist industry. Tourists like to see the horizon and the colours distract from their view.

title: Option: Seasonal Shutdown
text: Shutting down the wind turbines during peak migration seasons.
Excellent idea, if employed in combination with painting the rotor blades! It would even be better to install a radar system that automatically shuts down the turbines when birds are approaching.

if you combine this with the painting of the blades, I am confident that we would satisfy our obligations pursuant to the Ramsar and Bonn Conventions. It does however mean that the project generates up to 10% less energy, thereby threatening our progress towards SDG 13 and the Paris Agreement.

title: Option: Lower Turbines
text: Placing lower turbines to reduce the risk to birds.
Good idea! Lower turbines effectively remove the risks for birds.

This is a bad idea, as it seriously threatens our progress towards SDG 13 and the Paris Agreement, unless we place more wind turbines. Lower wind turbines will reduce the energy output of the project with 40%.
Placing more wind turbines would threaten the Ramsar site!
If the solution is placing more wind turbines, there is no future for Arcadian fishers.

title: Point of Interest: Wind Turbine Cluster (SDGs 1, 2, 8, 14)
text: The wind turbine cluster affects fishing livelihoods and marine biodiversity. Two key issues must be addressed.

title: Issue A: Fishing Grounds
text: Phase 1 — Exploration: Hear from the Fishers Guild, Legal Advisor, and AquaNautilus.

Fishing is deeply tied to the cultural identity and livelihood of Arcadian fishermen. Given our dependence on conventional fishing techniques (bottom-trawling) and limited economic alternatives, we are particularly vulnerable to the disruption caused by the wind park, as its underwater structures make fishing grounds unsuitable for bottom trawling.

Other suitable fishing grounds are too far removed from the coast and we do not have the means to adjust our fishing techniques to make them suitable for fishing in and around the site of the wind park. The project thus negatively impacts SDGs 1,2 and 8 and it violates our cultural rights and our rights to work and to an adequate standard of living.
The rights to work and an adequate standard of living entail best efforts obligations.

Nonetheless, the measures will make the fishers worse off and international human rights law formulates a strong presumption against regression. As for their cultural rights, it is debatable whether the use of specific fishing techniques is an intrinsic part of their culture.
We are concerned about the underwater noise and vibrations caused by the construction and operation of the wind parks.

This may affect the communication, navigation and feeding of marine mammals and fish and may even lead to habitat displacement. Without mitigating measures, the project will negatively impact SDG 14 and Arcadia will breach its environmental obligations under the UNCLOS.

Arcadia has an obligation to prevent, reduce and control pollution under Art. 194 UNCLOS. A key question is whether underwater noise falls under the definition of pollution under Article 1(1)(4) UNCLOS. If so, Art. 194 UNCLOS requires Arcadia to take measures to prevent, reduce and control the noise and vibrations, using the best practicable means at their disposal.

title: Issue A: Phase 2 — Intervention
text: Two options are available regarding the fishing grounds.

How would you like to 
address the impact on fishing?

options.label: Moving the wind park to a different location, further away from the coast
Facilitating the development of artificial reefs

title: Option: Move Wind Park
text: Moving the wind park to a different location, further away from the coast.
Thank you for giving priority to our interests!

We are strongly opposed to this option, as we need to put an end to the destructive bottom-trawling practices of the FishersGuild. In addition, from the moving the wind park away from the coast is even worse for marine biodiversity. It would threaten the breeding grounds of our seal colony. Please reconsider!
if you move the wind park, there is no other option than to position it outside our territorial sea. This is problematic, as we do not have full sovereignty over the EEZ.

title: Option: Artificial Reefs
text: Facilitating the development of artificial reefs as part of the wind park design.
Excellent idea! This will be a valuable habitat for numerous fish species, including the endangered Conan Cod. The abundance of fish will also attract species higher up the food chain, such as seals.

The reefs also create new opportunities for us. The reefs can be used as breeding grounds for oysters and mussels that could provide us with new sources of income. We will likewise benefit from the increase in fish in the immediate vicinity of the wind park.
The only problem is that we need to significantly adapt our fishing techniques. This is both expensive and requires training. Can you provide us financial compensation to help us transitioning?

Arcadia is not obliged to help the fishers transition, but it is good practice. The preamble of the Paris Agreement requests us to take into account the imperatives of a just transition of the workforce.

title: Issue B: Underwater Noise
text: Phase 2 — Intervention: Reducing underwater noise during construction.

Which method would you 
like to use to reduce 
underwater noise?

options.label: Using suction buckets as foundation for the wind turbines
Wrapping bubble curtains around the poles

title: Option: Suction Buckets
text: Using suction buckets as foundation for the wind turbines is an eco-friendly and experimental technique.

This is an eco-friendly and affordable option. However, as this is an experimental technique, I would advise against it, as little is known about its impact on the stability of the wind turbines in the long-term.
It may be an experimental technique, but it is the best option for marine life. You cannot always have scientific certainty. Sometimes you just need to stick your neck out.

title: Option: Bubble Curtains
text: Wrapping bubble curtains around the poles to dampen underwater noise.
This option is scientifically sound and without risks. It is therefore more in line with the precautionary principle, even though it’s more costly.
This is indeed the safest option, but it is more intrusive for marine life.

title: Point of Interest: Port (SDGs 8, 9, 13, 14)
text: The port is a key stakeholder. If ships need to make a detour, Arcadia's position as a global transport hub could be at risk.

title: Phase 1 — Exploration
text: Hear from the Port Authority, Legal Advisor, and AquaNautilus.
we welcome the project, as it will help the port to become more sustainable, thus contributing to SDG 9.

We are however concerned about our competitiveness: if ships need to make a detour to reach the port, they may prefer to go to Babylonia’s port instead and we may thus lose our position as a global transport hub.

The detour also negatively impacts SDGs 13 and 14, as it will increase the use of fuel by ships, causing higher emissions of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere and pollution to the marine environment. Arcadia will thus aggrevate its GHG emissions that it precisely seeks to reduce through this project. We believe that this cannot be Arcadia’s intention.
Arcadia has an obligation to prevent, reduce and control pollution of the marine environment under Art. 194 UNCLOS.

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea has determined that anthropogenic GHG emissions into the atmosphere constitute pollution of the marine environment within the meaning of Article 1(1)(4) UNCLOS. As for its climate obligations under the Paris Agreement, Arcadia has discretion as to how it reduces its GHG emissions, so long as the totality of its measures is ambitious and reflects its capacities.

title: Phase 2 — Intervention
text: Two options are available regarding the port.

What would you 
like to do about the port?

options.label: Leave the port where it is
Move the port to the island of Kalymera

title: Option: Leave Port
text: Leaving the port in its current location will result in longer shipping routes.
You do realise that you jeopardise Arcadia’s position as a global transport hub?
This is a bad idea, as the additional GHG emissions will negatively impact marine life.

title: Option: Move Port to Kalymera
text: Moving the port to the island of Kalymera. Costly but more sustainable in the long run.
We very much welcome your decision, as it will not only help us remain competitive, but it will also enable us to invest in new infrastructure that is more sustainable.
I do not have any concerns from a legal perspective, but do keep in mind that moving the port is a costly matter.
